rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer: North American Aviation built the spacecraft. Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". Columbia was part of the command and service module, which North American Aviation built [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The company was the prime contractor for that module [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the tank's heaters were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours, which emptied the tank. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The investigating board, the Apollo 13 Review Board chaired by Edgar Cortright, traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The thermostatic switches are the cause the board's report points to. The tank's description says its 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion. [[oxygen-tank-2]] description: "Apollo [unverified] 13 service module tank whose 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion"

rows.question: Which Apollo 11 crew member earned a doctorate on the kind of rendezvous Apollo relied on, and in which year?
rows.answer:
Buzz Aldrin, the Apollo 11 lunar module pilot, earned his MIT doctorate in 1963, with a thesis on manned orbital rendezvous [[buzz-aldrin]] "[stated] Earned an MIT doctorate in 1963 with a thesis on manned orbital rendezvous (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

Apollo relied on lunar orbit rendezvous, the mission mode NASA chose in 1962. A separate lander meets the mothership in lunar orbit [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "[stated] Required a separate lander, which became the lunar module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". It was chosen over direct ascent and Earth orbit rendezvous [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "[stated] Was chosen over direct ascent and Earth orbit rendezvous (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot. His exposure started the crew swap, which brought in Jack Swigert as Apollo 13 command module pilot in place of Ken Mattingly ([[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"; [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)").

Swigert was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office ([[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)").

The notes do not say how or when he died.

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was oxygen tank No. 2, a service module tank. Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air ([[command-service-module]] "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"). The oxygen tank note describes it as an Apollo 13 service module tank ([[oxygen-tank-2]] description: "Apollo [unverified] 13 service module tank whose 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion").

The command and service module was piloted by Michael Collins, according to the relationship links between the two notes ([[command-service-module]] link: "piloted [unverified] by [[michael-collins]]"). Collins was the Apollo 11 command module pilot ([[michael-collins]] "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)").

During the landing, Collins did not land on the Moon. He stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia ([[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)").

The notes do not contain a fact line stating that oxygen tank No. 2 was carried by the command and service module. That link comes only from the relationship map, so I am relying on the service-module fact above for it.

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The mailbox was an improvised CO2 scrubber adapter, made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

It was needed because the command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

Mission Control in Houston also designed the adapter. [[mission-control-houston]] "[stated] Engineers there devised the Apollo 13 carbon dioxide scrubber adapter (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The brain doesn't say which hoses, bags or tape were used, or give the step-by-step build procedure.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Apollo 13 dates in 1970, in order:

1. **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided and announced, and Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly as command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" and [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded, about 56 hours into the flight. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" The mission goal also changed from a lunar landing at Fra Mauro to a safe return to Earth, by a Mission Control abort decision. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17:** The crew splashed down after using the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970:** The Apollo 13 Review Board report was published. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" The report traced the fire to oxygen tank No. 2, which its own fact lines in [[apollo-13-review-board]] support: "[stated] [unverified] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The brain gives only the month for the June 1970 report, not a day.
